findings.title: A Table filter change wipes the Final Truth form's typed words and an unsaved Key limit override tick
findings.refuter_why: The same defect as D-1, with the same reading. It worked on 1eee4d62: the filter's change only refreshed, and live.mjs capture/restore (not changed by this release) carried the dirty final* fields and keyOverride by name. It fails on 14bb0d92 because saveDrawnForm marks them as drawn before that refresh.
findings.what_happens: Since this line a Table filter's change runs saveDrawnForm before the redraw. saveFieldsIn (investigation.mjs:1914-1929) takes every dirty [name] field of the window's form and calls keepDrawn on each, so each becomes 'as drawn', but applyDashboardSave writes only traces, Key rows and the schema: the Final Truth fields (finalRoom, finalVis, finalAuthor, finalName, finalText, finalAnalysis, finalNote) and keyOverride are written nowhere. The redraw's capture keeps only dirty fields (live.mjs:787), so the rebuilt Final Truth tab is drawn from `finalDraft` (null, or an older draft) and the override box unticked.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens the Investigation window on the Table, fills the Final Truth tab (room, name, words), goes to the Remnants tab and changes Order or the Chapter filter: the Final Truth tab now shows empty fields; Save or a close places nothing and asks nothing. On 1.2.121 the same filter change kept the typed fields (live.mjs carried them). Same for a ticked 'Place more than the opening roll allows' on the Key Remnants tab: it unticks and the Place buttons grey again.

findings.where: scripts/live.mjs:720-733 (keyFor's positional path), :250 (replaceQuietly), :660-673 (owedFrom, oweChange); scripts/float-text.mjs:193 (`el.before(hold)`); scripts/remnant-ring.mjs:456-462 (textareas with no name, key or id), :256-262 (watch tokens: true, whileEditing)
findings.title: The GM's Remnant card loses the words being typed in its two text boxes at every redraw, and saves nothing: float-text's placeholder moves the nameless textarea's key, and the R-1 guard now swallows the blur that used to save
findings.refuter_why: The real card matches the page the first reader built in every part that decides the outcome, and the outcome repeats with the real markup and the real wiring. The Remnant card is drawn into the trace's actor sheet by the renderActorSheetV2 hook (remnant-ring.mjs:196-204, showRemnantCard :229-264): body.innerHTML = gmRemnantCard(...), wireCardEditing(body), then keepLive with region '.drpg-remnant-card', watch { items: true, tokens: true, stores: [remnantStore] }, whileEditing true, after = wireCardEditing. Its two text boxes (remnant-ring.mjs:455-462) are `<textarea rows="3" data-drpg-public="playerText"|"analyzedText" data-drpg-was=... placeholder=...>` each alone in a `<label>` after a te
findings.what_happens: float-text lifts a focused textarea of an actor sheet (FLOAT_SCOPE includes .application.sheet.actor; the card is drawn in the trace's actor sheet) and puts a hidden placeholder before it in its label. The card's textareas have no name, data-drpg-key or id, so live.mjs keys them by position: index 1 in the old label (after the placeholder), 0 in the new one. At a redraw (any token update, create or delete in the world) capture keys the typed text and the focus under the old path, restore and giveFocusBack find no field there: the new textarea shows the stored words and the focus goes to the page. oweChange then finds no focused field and owes nothing, and the old field's blur, which saves the card, was swallowed by guardWindow. The words typed are gone and anything typed next goes to no field. On 1.2.121 the same redraw also lost the focus, but the old field's blur saved what had been typed (r121-R-1's premature save), so the words survived.
findings.failure_scenario: Daily Life: the GM opens a trace's card to rewrite what the players read and types while the students walk the map. At the next step the sentence vanishes from the box and the caret is gone; nothing reached the trace or the Truth Bullets. The GM clicks back in and starts again, and loses it again at the next step.

findings.title: A student who found a hidden stash with Analyze can no longer see or rifle it: the finder's browser no longer knows the stash exists
findings.refuter_why: Traced every row after a find. resolveStashSearch (GM) writes only the finder's found flag and whispers the finder and the GMs; it sends no copy (no tellHiddenStashes/sendTo call). Who holds the found stash's row afterwards: every GM (hiddenStashStore, synced; hiddenStashesAt reads it), the stash owner's players (rowsFor: owned actors), the Mastermind's players (rowsFor all). The finder's player does not: rowsFor filters actors by OWNER and never reads the found list, readersOf(actorId) names the stash owner's players and the Mastermind's, and receive keeps only what was sent. The region lists open stashes alone since 1190ab8a. So on the finder's browser stashesIn -> stashesOn -> openStashes
findings.what_happens: openStashesHere runs on the player's browser (the sheet's open-stash section, sheet-inventory.mjs:345; rifleStashDialog, stash-reach.mjs:281) and walks stashesIn(room), keeping a concealed entry only for the Mastermind or a finder (`hasFoundStash`). On 1.2.121 the hidden entry was on the region, so the finder's browser listed it. Since 1190ab8a the region keeps open stashes alone and stashesOn adds hidden ones from the player's copy, which holds only the player's own characters' rows (hidden-stashes.mjs:138-151 rowsFor, :116-120 readersOf). A finder who is not the stash's owner or the Mastermind never has the row, so the found stash is not listed and the Rifle says there is no open stash here. The GM side (stealFromVault) would still allow it, but no window sends it.
findings.failure_scenario: Botan beats 16 on Analyze - Locate a hidden stash in Chie's bedroom and is told he found it. His sheet shows no open stash there, and Rifle a stash says there is none, so the find gives him nothing.

findings.title: A third of an open (unmasked, direct) murder whose Escape Together fails is sent the hidden-defence card, '12 against 15 + a hidden defense: a miss', after their menu said 'Beat 16'
findings.refuter_why: On 1eee4d62 defenseHiddenFor spread the copy over the GMs' state (murder-rules.mjs 4411-4417 at v1.2.121), so a reader with an empty copy kept the GMs' killerId. Now killerId/victimId are the copy's alone (:4495-4501). A third whose Escape Together fails is unseated by thirdLeaves (:1968-1969) before the card; castCopyFor gives a user outside incidentAudienceIds {} or {betrayal} (incident-store.mjs:580), so killerId is null and crisisDefenseHidden (:284-287) is true for sharedEscape, whose defence is the killer's leg (config.mjs:4221-4223), in an open murder too. That third was seated with killerId kept (incident-store.mjs:591, neither indirect nor masked), so their menu showed the full numb
findings.what_happens: The r121-K-1 fix sets killerId and victimId from the reader's own copy alone. A third whose Escape Together failed has left (thirdLeaves, :1969) before the card, and castFor sends a reader with no seat {} (incident-store.mjs:581), so killerId is null and crisisDefenseHidden answers true for the killer-defended row whatever the incident: in a trap or behind a mask that is the fix, but in an open murder the third knew the killer, was shown the full number, and on 1eee4d62 was sent the full line. findings.title: The sheet's room watch redraws every rendered window whose document is a character - Configure Ownership and Daggerheart's character settings among them - on every token move and item change
findings.refuter_why: New in 1.2.122 (openCharacterSheets did not exist on 1eee4d62, and no hook redrew another window on another token's move). openCharacterSheets takes every rendered app whose document is a character; only onRenderCharacterSheet notes a signature, so Configure Ownership and Daggerheart's character settings are redrawn on every pass (any token x/y/elevation/hidden/actorId, any item change on a character, 60 ms trailing). The same release has isCharacterSheet (UI-09) and does not use it here. Foundry's own document.apps redraw already covered the same actor's updates; a stranger's step is what is new. The lost unsaved choice is Foundry's form redraw, unread on v14 - minor until read; major if co
findings.what_happens: openCharacterSheets takes any rendered application with `document.type === "character"`; redrawRoomSheets skips one only when ROOM_SIGNATURES holds an equal signature, and only onRenderCharacterSheet notes one. A window that is not the sheet is never noted, so every pass (any token's x, y, elevation, hidden or actor change, any item change on any character, after 60 ms) calls its render(false); a token made or taken away or a region written does the same for its scene. The same release's UI-09 names exactly these windows as 'another window of the same character' (window-scale.mjs isCharacterSheet), but the watch does not use that test.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens Configure Ownership for a student and changes two players' levels; before Save, a player steps their token: the window redraws from the stored ownership and the two choices are gone (as Foundry's form redraw is recalled; v14 not read). findings.title: A returning player's eight notices now go to the oldest of their returned cards, not the newest
findings.refuter_why: askForWords now marks every card asked and gives the slots to the first eight answers; the GM answers in the order of the ask's ids, which is game.messages order, the order the chat log draws as chronological, so the eight notices go to the oldest of the player's own cards. 1.2.121 sorted by timestamp, newest first, and took eight. No sort was found before the emit, in answerWordsRequest or in cardOnReturn. The comments at secret.mjs:1015 ('Only the newest RETURN_NOTICES of an ask raise one') and :1029 ('The newest cards of one ask') now say the opposite of the code. The 16 case needs a second primary's ready during the wait, which is narrow, but the main case is the ordinary return. R8103 m
findings.what_happens: askForWords marks every card asked (`for (const id of mine) noticeOnReturn.add(id)`) and sets returnNoticesLeft = 8; cardOnReturn raises a notice for the first 8 answers. `mine` is game.messages.contents in collection order (oldest first), the GM answers ids in that order (answerWordsRequest's `for (const id of ids)`) and emits one packet per card, so the first 8 answered are the 8 oldest. Until 1.2.121 the slots went to the newest 8 by timestamp. A second ask (another GM's ready, `ACTION_GM_READY` -> askForWords) resets the count to 8, so up to 16.
findings.failure_scenario: A player opens the game on a new browser (or after a long absence) with thirty private cards of their own: eight popups from the start of the season land in the middle of the screen and in the notice history; the cards of last night raise none.

findings.title: A masked killer whose name holds an apostrophe or an ampersand is named in clear on every card the mask's name cut is meant to cover: maskNames returns the words untouched when the raw name is not a substring of the escaped HTML
findings.refuter_why: Stands on the road the finding names, but narrower than 'every card'. maskNames (secret.mjs:567) returns early when no raw name is a substring of the html. A card whose words pass a DOM serialisation before the cut - playerWords (secret.mjs:381-388) when the card holds .drpg-gm-only or call-actions prose, cutWords (:597-614) when it holds youOrThem lines - reaches maskNames with an apostrophe or a double quote written raw again, so for O'Hara or a quoted nickname those cards are cut; a plain card (no GM prose, no you/them lines) is not. An ampersand stays & after serialisation, so a name with '&' is in clear on every card of the cut. The Frisk 'caught' line to the target's player (frisk.
findings.what_happens: wordsFor (secret.mjs:586-590) cuts a masked character's name to '?' for every reader outside the mask through maskNames. maskNames first asks `list.some(n => html.includes(n))` and returns the HTML unchanged when no raw name occurs in it. Every card writes names through foundry.utils.escapeHTML / esc, which turns ' into ' and & into & (the harness's futil.mjs:61-65 models the same), so a name like "Ren O'Hara" is in the HTML as "Ren O'Hara": the precheck fails and the DOM walk below it, which would have matched the decoded text, never runs. The cut is the one net the module relies on for a Frisk's, a Steal's, a Palm's and an onlooker's line (secret.mjs:461-464) and for words kept under a mask after it ends (heldMaskNames).
findings.failure_scenario: A direct murder opens on Hope, so Ren O'Hara is behind a '?'. Later that time of day Ren Frisks a student; the Frisk's card to that student's player passes wordsFor, the cut returns the words as written, and the player reads 'Ren O'Hara' - the killer the mask hides. The same for any card on the cut's road and for a card's words served again after the mask lapsed without a reveal.

findings.title: A node pressed in the trial console's schema does not open that node when the Investigation's Map already stands: the Map is only raised
findings.refuter_why: openInvestigationDashboard returns RAISED at its first line when a drpg-window-case window is rendered (investigation.mjs:2443), before node or view is read, so a press with the Map standing only raises it. findings.title: Season setup's scenes part does not draw a student added to the world while it stands, and its nine hooks stay until the next scene, region or setting event after the window closes
findings.refuter_why: followRoles registers clientSettingChanged, updateSetting/createSetting and six scene/region hooks; no createActor/deleteActor, and its comment says a student added meanwhile is not drawn. off() runs only inside alive(), which runs only when one of those hooks fires, so the hooks outlive a closed window until such an event; the comment's 'The hooks go when the window does' overstates it. The listeners are cheap and self-removing, so the residue is the undrawn student against the owner's live-window rule.
findings.what_happens: followRoles follows another GM's school, hall, zones and cast ticks, but a student created meanwhile is drawn only when the window opens again (its own comment), against the owner's rule that a window redraws at once on any change. Its hooks are taken off only inside alive(), which runs when one of the hooks fires, so a closed window leaves its listeners registered until such an event.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs prepare a season; one creates a new student while the other has Season setup's scenes part open. The new student has no cast tick until Season setup is closed and opened again.

findings.title: The describe window's clock closes it under a GM who is still typing, and drops what was typed
findings.refuter_why: The clock is one setTimeout of waitMs (TIMING.rulingMs = 180000, config.mjs:384). Nothing resets it: no input or focus listener touches `timer`. At the end it closes the window and answers null (observe.mjs:1321-1327, 1429-1432), and the primary's callback, which would read the fields, never runs. The GM's words are dropped and the timed-out toast tells them to add the words in the Investigation window. Minor: it needs more than three minutes in one describe window, and the find itself still lands.
findings.what_happens: describeFind races the window against a fixed TIMING.rulingMs (180 s) timer that is not reset by input; at the end it closes the window and answers null, so the find goes out under the prefilled name and the words typed in the window are not read.

On a player, murderState() is the world setting merged with readCast() (incident-store.mjs:189-192), and the player's cast is that user's GM-store copy (settings.mjs:3606, readMine), which comes in its own packet (incident-store.mjs castPacket/sendCast) and is kept in client storage across a reload (gm-store.mjs:1432-1449). Th

A copy that holds the incident at its earlier stage (the stage update still on its way when the invitation lands) skips the wait, the loop's first openingStillWanted is false and the function returns null with no word to the GMs, as before.

findings.title: The empty room's ruling card, now posted by the GM, goes to the character's first owner's thread, not to the co-owner who asked
findings.refuter_why: scoreObserve's nothingHere branch runs on the primary GM and calls callGm(actor, { ...call, onPosted }) with no `thread` (observe.mjs:885). observeRulingCall's return carries none, and callGm reads threadOf(actor, thread) (call-gm.mjs:958). With no asker and a GM poster, threadOf falls back to ownerOf (:1030-1034). The asker is on the row (entry.by, observe.mjs:222). Other questions the primary holds pass `thread: ctx.asker` (call-gm.mjs:259, 292, 354, 425), so the omission is real. It matters only for characters with more than one owner.
findings.what_happens: scoreObserve's nothingHere branch calls callGm on the primary GM's browser with no `thread`; threadOf then sees a GM poster and falls back to ownerOf (call-gm.mjs:1025-1033). The row holds the asker (`entry.by`). Until this line the player's own browser posted the card, which under 1.2.122's COMM-25 rule goes to the asker's thread.

findings.title: A player's token settings are refused only the first time a given window renders; a token's cached sheet opened again is shown
findings.refuter_why: No close hook, render-state check or delete takes a window out of refusedConfigs; Foundry keeps one sheet object per token document, so the second double right-click renders the same object and passes. The test pins the hole as intended behaviour (the second call on the same app answers false). Minor: Trusted players only (TOKEN_CONFIGURE), against the owner's D-A11, v14 reuse unread.
findings.what_happens: refuseTokenConfig keeps every window it refused in a WeakSet and answers false, doing nothing, for a window in that set. The set was meant to stop the two render hooks of one render closing a window twice, but it is never cleared, and Foundry keeps one sheet object per token document (TokenDocument#sheet, as recalled for v13; v14 not read). The second double right-click of a Trusted player on their own token renders the same TokenConfig object again: it is in the set, so it is neither hidden nor closed.
